This year's competition for the Tom Carter Cup clashed with the last British League Match and not surprisingly the field was short of our Surrey 10000m champion - Oliver Foote plus other middle distance specialists.

But pride of place must go to Oliver Foote who took the field apart as he moved from scratch through to take the lead at Wimbledon Village after which he coasted to a 9 sec. lead.

Like the Curate's egg the Cross Country season was good in parts, initially promising a lot with a win in the South of Thames Junior, but turning out to be a lame effort with only Oliver Foote in the Seniors and Andy North in the Juniors showing impressive improvements with high placings in the National CC Champs.
Oliver Foote was on schedule to lead the individual championship but was on holiday for the last match. Notable improvements from Andy North, Martin Lake and Francis Ward.

Oliver Foote dropped out (the start of five) but Dave North showed good form while Mike Hayes returned to competition after illness and gradually worked through the field to finish in a creditable position.

But pride of place went again to Oliver Foote. Not known to like muddy courses he had a battle royal with Karl Harrison (who was to feature so well in 10k Road Races in the summer) with Karl finishing in 56th place and Oliver in 59th.
